answer: The predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR with treatment in patients aged 65 is approximately 0.395 (39.5%). Model: unregularized logistic regression (statsmodels Logit, n=80; 41 PR vs 39 SD/PD, no CR values present) with age as the only predictor: logit(P) = 4.446565 − 0.074954·Age. Age coefficient −0.07495 (SE 0.02435, p=0.0021; OR per year 0.928) is significant, indicating older age reduces PR probability. At Age=65 the linear predictor is −0.4254, giving P(PR|65) = 1/(1+e^0.4254) = 0.3952 (95% CI ≈ 0.273–0.532). Caveat: the Groups column is perfectly confounded with outcome (Group 1 = 41 PR, Group 2 = 39 SD/PD), so it cannot serve as a treatment/control filter and was excluded; all 80 records are treated as the treated cohort per the question.
